title: Lorlatinib therapy
purpose: Lorlatinib aims to control ALK-positive advanced lung cancer, including disease in the brain where present. Your oncology team explains the likely benefit, treatment line and alternatives for your situation.
context_label: ALK-positive advanced NSCLC · specified later-line NCCP indication; separate licensed first-line context
scope_note: This guide covers lorlatinib alone for ALK-positive advanced non-small-cell lung cancer. The available Irish NCCP v3 document lists use after particular earlier ALK medicines. The current European licence also includes people who have not had an ALK inhibitor. The team must confirm your treatment setting and the current Irish protocol and access arrangements before prescribing; the source versions currently disagree.
schedule_summary: Lorlatinib is taken once daily continuously, with no planned rest week. Treatment continues while it is helping and side effects remain acceptable; there is no fixed number of treatment cycles.
administration_text: The usual starting dose is 100 mg once daily; use the dose on your prescription. Take it at about the same time each day, with or without food. Swallow whole; do not crush, chew or split tablets, or use damaged tablets. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.
indication_text: This guide covers lorlatinib alone for ALK-positive advanced non-small-cell lung cancer. The available Irish NCCP v3 document lists use after particular earlier ALK medicines. The current European licence also includes people who have not had an ALK inhibitor. The team must confirm your treatment setting and the current Irish protocol and access arrangements before prescribing; the source versions currently disagree.
monitoring_summary: Before starting: ALK testing, blood count, kidney and liver tests, clotting tests, cholesterol and triglycerides, glucose, pancreatic enzymes, blood pressure and an ECG. Lipids are checked at weeks 2, 4 and 8, then as needed. Blood count, kidney/liver tests, ECG and pancreatic enzymes are normally checked monthly. Blood pressure is checked after two weeks and at least monthly; glucose as needed. Scans follow your oncology plan.
urgent_extra: Contact your oncology team promptly for changes in memory, thinking, mood, speech or behaviour, hallucinations, new or worsening breathlessness, cough, fainting, a slow or irregular heartbeat, severe abdominal pain, marked thirst or frequent urination. Severe confusion, unsafe behaviour, severe breathing difficulty or collapse needs emergency help. Do not wait for the next appointment.
consent_support: Discuss the individual treatment setting, likely benefit and uncertainty, alternatives including not proceeding, brain/mood, metabolic, cardiac and lung risks, possible lasting effects, daily tablets, interactions, pregnancy/fertility and the monitoring/contact plan. Confirm the current Irish source/access discrepancy with the clinical team. This aid supports an ongoing consent conversation.

agents.name: Lorlatinib
agents.explanation: Lorlatinib blocks the abnormal ALK protein that helps some lung cancers grow. It can reach the brain, an important site of disease in ALK-positive lung cancer. It is selected using an ALK test. It can also affect healthy tissues, so blood tests and symptom checks remain important.
visual: Cancer growth may be controlled, including in the brain
agents.watch: Report thinking, mood, speech, breathing or heart symptoms promptly and attend lipid, glucose and other monitoring.
risks: Raised cholesterol and triglycerides; pancreatic inflammation may occur
Changes in memory, thinking, mood, speech or perception, including serious psychiatric effects
Heart conduction problems, fainting and reduced heart function
High blood pressure and raised blood sugar
Lung inflammation that can be serious
Harm to an unborn baby, contraception interactions and possible impaired male fertility

questions.q: Why is an ALK test needed?
questions.a: Lorlatinib is intended for cancers with a specific ALK change. Your team checks the result and whether the treatment fits your previous medicines.

questions.q: How long will I take it?
questions.a: Lorlatinib is taken once daily continuously, with no planned rest week. Treatment continues while it is helping and side effects remain acceptable; there is no fixed number of treatment cycles.

questions.q: What if I miss a dose or vomit?
questions.a: If a dose is missed, take it when remembered if the next dose is at least four hours away; otherwise skip it. Do not take two doses together. If you vomit after a dose, do not take another tablet; take the next dose at the usual time. These instructions follow the current product leaflet.

questions.q: Why are cholesterol tests needed if I feel well?
questions.a: Blood fats can rise without symptoms. Regular tests let the team treat this early. Raised cholesterol does not always mean lorlatinib must stop; your clinician uses the actual results and your overall condition.

questions.q: What changes should my family or friends notice?
questions.a: Changes in memory, concentration, mood, speech, behaviour or perceptions should be reported promptly. Agree with the team and someone you trust how changes will be noticed, if helpful.
Lorlatinib can affect thinking and other CNS functions. Use caution and discuss driving or operating machinery, particularly if symptoms occur.

questions.q: Does a dose reduction mean treatment has failed?
questions.a: No. A hold or reduction may allow side effects to recover and reduce harm. The team reviews cancer control separately and explains the restart plan.

questions.q: What belongs in the consent discussion?
questions.a: Discuss your aim, expected benefits and uncertainty, reasonable alternatives including not proceeding, serious and lasting risks, daily practicalities, contraception, fertility, support needs and your right to reconsider.

phases.detail: Lorlatinib is taken once daily continuously, with no planned rest week. Treatment continues while it is helping and side effects remain acceptable; there is no fixed number of treatment cycles.

support.title: Taking and replacing tablets
support.text: If a dose is missed, take it when remembered if the next dose is at least four hours away; otherwise skip it. Do not take two doses together. If you vomit after a dose, do not take another tablet; take the next dose at the usual time. These instructions follow the current product leaflet.

support.title: Cholesterol and other medicines
support.text: Cholesterol or triglycerides may rise without symptoms. Attend blood tests and take any prescribed lipid-lowering medicine. Ask the pharmacist before starting or stopping any medicine, supplement or herbal product, including St John’s wort. Do not change the lorlatinib dose yourself.

support.title: Sickness and daily wellbeing
support.text: This oral regimen has minimal to low sickness risk. Use anti-sickness medicine only according to your own plan and report persistent vomiting or poor intake. A standard chemotherapy steroid or anti-sickness course is not automatically needed.

support.title: Thinking, mood and practical support
support.text: Ask someone you trust to help notice changes in thinking, mood, speech or behaviour, if you wish. Report changes early. Lorlatinib can affect driving and machine use, especially when CNS effects are present; discuss whether it is safe for you.

support.title: Pregnancy, fertility and feeding
support.text: Lorlatinib may harm an unborn baby and make hormonal contraception less effective. Women who could become pregnant need highly effective non-hormonal contraception during treatment and for at least 35 days afterwards; discuss any unavoidable hormonal method and barrier protection. Men with partners who could become pregnant need effective contraception including a condom during treatment and for at least 14 weeks afterwards; condoms are also needed with a pregnant partner. Discuss fertility preservation before treatment. Do not breastfeed during treatment; agree when it can safely resume with the team.

evidence.title: Evidence differs before and after earlier ALK treatment
evidence.intro: A first-line randomised trial and separate later-line cohorts answer different questions.
evidence.population: ALK-positive advanced NSCLC; untreated patients in CROWN and previously treated patients in the global phase 2 study.
evidence.comparison_label: Crizotinib in CROWN; no comparator in phase 2
evidence.interpretation: The first-line CROWN trial found longer control of cancer and brain progression with lorlatinib than with crizotinib. Separate studies showed activity after earlier ALK medicines. Outcomes depend on the treatment setting and cannot predict one person’s benefit; the treatments have different monitoring and side-effect burdens.
evidence.limitations: First-line and later-line results are not interchangeable. Current evidence does not provide a personal prognosis or a direct comparison against every other ALK treatment.
